name: Standard Scramble
approach: Via the North Fork Quinault Trailhead (North Shore Road), hike the North Fork Quinault River Trail roughly 16 miles to Low Divide — fords at Wild Rose Creek, Elip Creek, and 16-Mile Creek can be difficult or impassable in high water — then follow the primitive, unmaintained Skyline Ridge Trail toward Promise Creek Pass before dropping off-trail onto Lawson's slopes.
firstResearcherNote: Sixteen Mile base; route text also mentions Low Divide and the Skyline trail, so the exact line is uncertain; the Elip Creek group entry duplicates listed camps.

camps.name: Sixteen Mile Camp — the base directly under Mount Lawson
camps.notes: This is the camp for MOUNT LAWSON and effectively the only one. The peak rises about 3,800 ft above the river in a mile and a third, straight out of the drainage the camp sits in, and the climb is a c…

name: West Route
approach: Two common trailheads reach the base: (1) Andrews Creek Trailhead (Trail 504) — from Winthrop, take Hwy 20 to County Road 1213/West Chewuch Road, drive ~6 miles to Forest Road 51, continue ~22 miles to the trailhead at road's end (3,050 ft). Hike via Andrews Pass and the Boundary Trail to Upper Cathedral Lake (roughly 7 hours for a loaded backpacking pace). (2) Chewuch River Trail/Thirtymile Trailhead — a longer approach (about 20 miles and ~4,900 ft gain to Upper Cathedral Lake), also joining near Cathedral Pass. Most parties backpack in and camp at or near Upper Cathedral Lake (~7,380 ft) be…
firstResearcherNote: Upper Cathedral Lake is standard; unsure whether the West Route actually passes through the Amphitheater upper basin, kept as onRoute.

camps.name: Upper Cathedral Lake basin
camps.notes: The working climbers' camp for both the Southeast Buttress and Amphitheater's ridges, sitting directly under the peaks with short walks to either. The basin has taken heavy use for decades and the For…

camps.name: Andrews Pass
camps.notes: The natural first-night stop if you leave the trailhead in the afternoon, roughly twelve miles up the drainage and about the halfway mark to the Cathedral basin. Everything below here is BURN — the lo…

camps.name: Remmel Lake and the Spanish Camp meadows
camps.notes: This sits a short way off the main line to Cathedral Pass and works well as a base if Remmel Mountain is on the list alongside Cathedral and Amphitheater. The meadow ground is soft and easily damaged,…

camps.name: Cathedral Pass benches and the tarn slabs
camps.notes: Useful mainly as a high, quick bivy if you arrive late or want to be moving before dawn, since it saves the drop into the lake basin and puts you already at the crest. The ground is rock and thin turf…

camps.name: Amphitheater Mountain upper basin
camps.notes: Reached by following the trail southeast around Amphitheater's west ridge from Upper Cathedral Lake and then a boot path up scree and grass into the basin. Worth considering only if you want to be on …

name: Standard Route (South Ridge / South Gully via Copper Glance Basin)
approach: From Winthrop, drive north about 8 miles on West Chewuch Road (County Road 1213) to Eightmile Road (Forest Road 5130), then continue roughly 12-15 miles northwest along Eightmile Creek to the Copper Glance Trailhead (about 3,800-3,810 ft; no fee). Hike Copper Glance Trail #519, which begins on an old mining-claim jeep track/tramway grade (FSR 505) for about 1.5 miles to the historic Copper Glance mine, crosses Copper Glance Creek (the creek's bridge has been reported washed out or missing in some years, requiring a ford), and continues through a 2018 burn area past a small pond to Copper Glanc…
firstResearcherNote: Unsure whether the 6,600 ft basin waypoint is a separate spot above the lake or the same camp.

camps.name: Copper Glance Lake
camps.notes: This is the only camp that serves Big Craggy and West Craggy, and it belongs to a different drive from everything else in this zone: north from Winthrop on the West Chewuch road, then left onto the Ei…

name: Southeast Ridge
approach: From Winthrop, drive Highway 20 west about 14-15 miles to the Mazama junction, then either (a) continue on Lost River Road (County Road 9140) about 8.75 miles (paved then gravel Forest Road 5400) to Robinson Creek Trailhead, or (b) turn onto the Harts Pass Road (also FR-5400) and drive about 9.0 miles to the same trailhead (elev. ~2,500-2,560 ft, with an information sign, picnic table, and vault toilet). From the trailhead, hike the Robinson Creek - Middle Fork Trail (#478) south for about 2.8 miles to the signed/bridged Beauty Creek junction (elev. ~3,560 ft) just past a bridge over Beauty Cr…
firstResearcherNote: Added the Beauty Creek tarn as main; unsure whether the Robinson Creek valley entry already means this tarn.

camps.name: Beauty Creek tarn camp
camps.notes: Leave the Robinson Creek trail for the Beauty Creek path, then take the steep boot path up to the tarn below the southeast cirque. The meadows between Robinson and Beauty Peak also have space.

camps.name: Robinson Creek valley campsites
camps.notes: The trailhead sits at about 2,560 feet just off the Harts Pass road, which means this is the low road into country whose summits stand near 8,500 — the elevation gain is the whole story. Robinson Moun…

name: Windy Peak via Windy Creek Trail (Cathedral Driveway Approach)
approach: From Loomis, drive Toats Coulee Road (FR-39) roughly 22 miles to Long Swamp Campground, then continue about 3 more miles west on FR-39 to the Cathedral Driveway trailhead. The final stretch of road is gravel but reported as smooth/passenger-car friendly.
firstResearcherNote: Uncertain: this is mostly a day hike and no listed camp is on the Windy Creek trail, so the added plateau camp is a best guess.

camps.name: Windy Peak south plateau
camps.notes: Usually done as a day hike. Parties who split it camp on the open south slopes and plateau below the summit, where this trail joins the standard route.

name: Indian Summer
approach: Western approach (the recommended option): roughly 10 miles with about 7,800 ft of gain via the Ptarmigan Traverse trail toward Spire Point — described as a 'brutal approach' with significant bushwhacking. A longer eastern approach via Chelan also exists but adds a full extra day each way.
firstResearcherNote: South-face rock route on Dome from the western approach; camp at Itswoot Ridge or the Dome Glacier high bivies is inferred from the standard Dome approach, not confirmed for this rarely repeated line.

camps.name: Itswoot Ridge
camps.notes: This is the working base for the southern peaks and the camp most parties coming in from Downey Creek actually use. Camps are quoted anywhere between roughly 5,900 and 6,400 ft depending on which benc…

camps.name: Dome Glacier and Dome-Chickamin col high bivouacs
camps.notes: These are the camps that put the eastern peaks in range, and they are the reason parties carry a full glacier kit past Itswoot Ridge. The col between the Dana and Dome glaciers holds a couple of rock …

camps.name: Bachelor Creek forest and meadow camps
camps.notes: This exists because of the brush, and the brush is the single most important thing to understand about the south end. From the Downey Creek trailhead at 1,440 ft the Downey Creek trail runs about six …

camps.name: Cub Lake
camps.notes: Roughly 12 miles and about 3,900 ft of gain from the Downey Creek trailhead, reached by a steep switchbacking descent off the Bachelor Creek meadows and a walk around the north shore. Parties report a…

name: East Side Route
firstResearcherNote: Approach text is empty; assumed the north-end Ptarmigan Traverse approach from Cascade Pass, with Yang Yang Lakes the natural base and White Rock Lakes the option for traverse parties already past the Le Conte Glacier.

camps.name: Yang Yang Lakes
camps.notes: The second camp for most north-to-south parties, sitting in a shallow bowl below Le Conte Mountain after the drop off the Middle Cascade Glacier. It is the natural base for Old Guard Peak, whose summi…

camps.name: White Rock Lakes
camps.notes: The third camp and the one most parties remember, reached from Yang Yang across the Le Conte Glacier and the Le Conte-Sentinel col, then down a long traverse under Sentinel and Old Guard. It looks str…

camps.name: Kool-Aid Lake
camps.notes: The first camp on the traverse coming from Cascade Pass, reached by climbing to Cache Col and dropping a short but awkward distance southwest to the tarn. It is where the permit regime changes, which …

name: Northwest Buttress
approach: Drive to the Upper Dungeness Trailhead (Trail #833.2) in Olympic National Forest: from US 101 near Sequim Bay State Park turn onto Louella Road, continue about a mile to Palo Alto Road and turn left for roughly 1.1 miles to the forest boundary, where Palo Alto becomes Forest Service Road 28. Turn right on FS 2880, pass Dungeness Forks Campground, then stay left on FS 2870 for 8.7 miles to the trailhead just across the Dungeness River bridge (47.877572, -123.136927). There is a large parking area and a vault toilet but no potable water; a Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is required. H…
firstResearcherNote: Stored approach is the Upper Dungeness trail, so Home Lake is the base with Boulder Shelter on the way; not confirmed for this rarely climbed buttress.

camps.name: Home Lake, below Constance Pass — inside the park, and reached from the north
camps.notes: The high camp for both Warrior Peak and the northwest side of Inner Constance, and the natural next step up from Boulder Shelter once you want to be closer to the peaks. Reach it from the UPPER DUNGEN…

camps.name: Boulder Shelter — the last camp outside the national park
camps.notes: The working base for Warrior Peak, and the cheapest night in this zone by a wide margin because nothing has to be booked. It sits at about 4,950 ft and roughly 6.3 miles from the Upper Dungeness trail…

name: Ragged Ridge
firstResearcherNote: Fisher Camp kept on the assumption that the traverse exits down Fisher Creek; the exit varies.

camps.name: Mesahchie basin, below the col
camps.notes: This is the base for Mesahchie and the usual first night of any Ragged Ridge traverse. From Easy Pass the line goes cross-country west-northwest, sidehilling on heather and tiresome scree at around si…

camps.name: Ragged Ridge crest bivy, south of Mesahchie Col
camps.notes: This is the higher and more committing of the two Ragged Ridge camps, about a mile west-northwest of Easy Pass. Two ways reach it: sidehill west at roughly six thousand eight hundred feet on heather a…

camps.name: Easy Pass trailhead, SR 20
camps.notes: This is the only practical trailhead for Mesahchie, Katsuk, Kimtah and Mount Arriva, and it is worth understanding what the walk in costs before committing to it. The trail climbs roughly three thousa…

camps.name: Fisher Camp, Fisher Creek basin
camps.notes: Fisher Camp sits in the forested basin west of and well below Easy Pass, reached by carrying on over the pass and descending into Fisher Creek. It is the comfortable option and it is also the alternat…

name: Standard Route (Southeast Ridge via Jackita Ridge / Crater Lake Trail)
approach: From the Canyon Creek Trailhead (1,900 ft) on SR 20 (32.8 mi east of Marblemount / 55.1 mi west of Winthrop), take Jackita Ridge Trail #738, fording Canyon Creek and Granite Creek near the start. The trail climbs steeply through timber via numerous switchbacks (roughly 55) gaining about 3,400 ft over 4 miles to a junction near 5,000-5,260 ft, with views opening onto Crater and Jack Mountains above timberline. Turn left/west onto the Crater Lake Trail (brushy, user-maintained) for about a mile to Crater Lake basin (~5,000-5,700 ft) below the peak's south side.
firstResearcherNote: The camp for this route is Crater Lake, which was missing; Devils Park is on the Jackita Ridge trail beyond the junction. Crater Lake elevation not confirmed, so omitted.

camps.name: Crater Lake, below Crater Mountain
camps.notes: Small tarn at the base of the south ridge, about 1.1 miles past the Crater Mountain junction on the Jackita Ridge trail. Parties splitting the climb camp on the rocky ground just above it; many do the…

name: Northeast Glacier
approach: North from May Creek; northeast face of mountain via glacier approach
firstResearcherNote: Sparse record; assumed to share the Nohokomeen approach from May Creek, so it gets the same camps.

camps.name: High camp below the Nohokomeen Glacier
camps.notes: Most parties climb straight up from the lake trail on day one and camp high on the ridge below the toe of the Nohokomeen Glacier, roughly 5,200 ft, to leave a manageable summit day. Some camp higher o…

camps.notes: Designated camp on the East Bank Trail about 8 miles from the East Bank trailhead, where climbers leave the trail for the north side of Jack Mountain. It can also be reached by water taxi. Used as a f…

name: South Face / Southeast Ridge
approach: From the Canyon Creek Trailhead on SR-20 (about 16 miles west of Rainy Pass, elevation ~1,900ft), cross Canyon Creek on a log/plank crossing (can wash out in high water, check current conditions) and follow the Crater Lake/Jackita Ridge Trail (FST 738) as it climbs steeply through forest — roughly 3,400ft of gain in about 4 miles — to the Crater Mountain Trail (FST 746) junction near McMillan Park. Take FST 746 toward Crater Lake (~2,000ft of gain, about 2.3 hours in); this stretch has long, hot, dry switchbacks with no reliable water, so carry what you need from Canyon Creek. Around 6,700–7,2…
firstResearcherNote: A party record camps at the 6,000 ft basin WNW of point 7001 after passing Jerry Lakes; order of the two mains is a judgment call, and whether these camps are in Ross Lake NRA or the Pasayten Wilderness is not confirmed.

camps.notes: PLANNED camp and the standard staging point for the south face, on a heather bench above Crater Creek northwest of point 7001. Reached in roughly eight hours and eleven miles from the car, after the J…

camps.name: Jerry Lakes basin
camps.notes: PLANNED camp, a grassy boulder-strewn bowl with several separate sites; the best of them sits by the small lake between the two large ones. Snow-free by mid-August. It is the more pleasant camp of the…

name: Southwest Ridge
approach: Park at the Panther Creek / East Bank trailhead on SR 20 near milepost 138 (~1,800 ft), 18.5 miles east of Newhalem. Follow the East Bank Trail 2.4 miles west to a multi-way junction, then take the rightmost branch — the old Little Jack Trail, built by the Forest Service in the early 1900s for pack-animal grazing on the mountain's meadows. This climbs steadily to Little Jack at 6.0 miles from the car, gaining roughly 4,800 ft from the junction to the 6,745 ft summit. From Little Jack, continue north along the ridge crest to the notch, then traverse across to the base of Jack Mountain proper an…
firstResearcherNote: Added the Little Jack knoll camp; water there and which side of the boundary it sits on are not confirmed, and fast parties do the route car-to-car.

camps.name: Little Jack camp, knoll northwest of Little Jack
camps.notes: High camp on a small hump just northwest of Little Jack, reached by the old Little Jack trail from the East Bank trailhead. It looks straight across the head of Crater Creek at Jack Mountain and is th…

name: Standard Scramble
approach: From the Libby Lake Trailhead (a.k.a. Libby Creek Trailhead, ~4,430 ft; no parking fee or pass required at this trailhead) at the end of Libby Creek Road, follow Libby Creek Trail No. 415 southwest into the Lake Chelan–Sawtooth Wilderness. The trail climbs gradually through mixed conifer forest and crosses several tributaries of Libby Creek on logs or hoppable rocks (trekking poles help); tread can be brushy/overgrown in the lower stretches. The first reliable water is North Fork Libby Creek at roughly 3 miles. At about 5 miles you reach a decaying historic line cabin in a clearing — the key j…
firstResearcherNote: Parties camp at the old cabin or at Libby Lake just above; the cabin camp was missing. Its water source is assumed, not confirmed.

camps.name: Libby Lake
camps.notes: The camp for both Raven Ridge routes and the usual base for Hoodoo Peak. Getting here is a different drive from the Twisp River trailheads: from Twisp go east on Highway 20 then south on Highway 153 a…

camps.name: Old cabin camp, Libby Creek trail
camps.notes: Camp by the old 1900s cabin about 5 miles up the Libby Creek trail, just below Libby Lake. A common base for Hoodoo: the scramble starts up the boulder field and gully from here.

name: Southeast Ridge (Crater Lake Approach)
approach: From Twisp, take Highway 20 south ~2 miles to WA-153, then south on WA-153 to County Rd 1029 (Gold Creek Loop), continuing onto County Rd 1034 (Gold Creek Road), which becomes Forest Road 4340 after about 6 miles. Turn onto FR 4340-300 (Crater Creek Road) and follow it about 4.6 miles to the Crater Creek Trailhead (~4,750 ft; day-use fee $5, or $30/yr — Northwest Forest Pass/interagency passes accepted). Hike the Crater Creek/Crater Lakes Trail about 3.9 miles one-way, gaining roughly 2,200 ft, to Crater Lake, then continue off-trail up the southeast ridge to the ~8,000 ft col and on to the su…
firstResearcherNote: Added Crater Lakes as the camp for this approach; elevation not confirmed, and the route is often done in a day.

camps.name: Crater Lakes, Crater Creek trail
camps.notes: Lakes at the head of the Crater Creek trail from the Crater Creek trailhead. The natural camp for the southeast ridge; many parties do the route in a day.

name: Standard Scramble
approach: Two trailheads reach Cooney Lake and the SE Ridge. (1) Foggy Dew Trailhead (end of FR 4340-200, 3,400 ft) — from Twisp, take SR 20 east ~2 mi, then SR 153 south ~12 mi, then Gold Creek Loop Rd/County Rd 1034 and FR 4340 to the FR 4340-200 spur. Hike Foggy Dew Creek Trail #417 up the North Fork through Merchants Basin, then Cooney Lake Trail #434 to Cooney Lake (~7,200 ft); climb to Cooney Pass and the SE Ridge from there. Round trip is roughly 19 miles with about 5,560 ft of gain (a logged trip report took ~5.5 hr up, ~3 hr down). (2) Eagle Lakes/Crater Creek Trailhead (also off FR 4340, 4,700…
firstResearcherNote: Cooney Lake is the standard base; Upper Eagle Lake is only on the way for parties doing the Eagle Lakes loop, a judgment call.

camps.name: Upper Eagle Lake and Horsehead Pass
camps.notes: The hub of the southern Sawtooth and the practical base for Switchback Mountain, with Hoodoo and Raven Ridge also within reach along the crest. Access is the Gold Creek side, not the Twisp River: turn…

name: Northwest Arete
grade: Grade III-IV, Class 4-5 (mixed rock and snow)
approach: Two realistic approach options both start by parking at the lower White Salmon lodge on SR 542 (White Salmon Road, FR-3075) and following a dirt road up the White Salmon Creek drainage for under a mile. The more direct option drops off-trail across White Salmon Creek and climbs to the ridgecrest directly opposite the ski area, then follows the ridgecrest to the base of the mountain's north side. The alternative continues up the road as far as it goes, then travels off-trail up the valley until open slopes allow access to the lower White Salmon Glacier. From there, gain the crest of the northwe…
firstResearcherNote: No bivy record found for the arete; assumed to use the shared White Salmon approach ridge and bivy, which is uncertain.

camps.name: North Face bivy, where the rib meets the face
camps.notes: North Face parties share the early approach with the White Salmon Glacier route through a brushy section before the two diverge, and the usual bivy sits near 5,500 ft where the rib abuts the face, abo…

camps.notes: Camping above the chimneys is what makes Fisher Chimneys a comfortable two- or three-day climb rather than a very long push, and it puts the party above the loose, route-finding-heavy section for summ…

name: Price Glacier
approach: Trailhead is the Nooksack Cirque Trail #750, reached via Ruth Creek Road (FS-32) off the Mount Baker Highway near the Hannegan Pass Road junction. The first obstacle is Ruth Creek itself, which has no bridge at the trailhead — cross on a large logjam/log crossing just downstream, then pick up the trail on the far bank at the registry box; in early summer or after rain the ford/log crossing can be unsafe and has turned parties back. From there follow the old roadbed about 2 miles through old growth to the original trailhead site, then continue along the North Fork Nooksack River — gravel bars w…
firstResearcherNote: Parties bivy on the slabs or saddle above Price Lake below the glacier; descent route varies, so the Fisher Chimneys camps as on-route is a judgment call.
